sources.title: Altered Dopamine Metabolism and Response to Treatment with Levodopa/Carbidopa in MCT8 Deficiency
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text and displayed tables; linked supporting files/videos not separately inspected by root.
observations: The body distinguishes ten phenotyped patients from nine evaluable treatment courses; one died before response assessment.
Broad benefit is described in seven of nine, GMFM improvement in five of eight, and CGI-I improvement in six of nine; these endpoints and denominators are not interchangeable.
Functional-category scales did not show congruent improvement, some motor scores declined, and dystonia scores increased. Follow-up beyond three months is limited to subsets.
sources.interpretation: The paper supports a hypothesis of useful symptomatic benefit and an informative controlled comparison, not a pooled response probability or established disease modification.
limits: Uncontrolled observations and assessor/caregiver expectations remain material.
The abstract's7/10 shorthand is not used as a clean treated-person response rate.
Same document independently read by the human-evidence agent; no additional evidence family.

sources.title: Healing Diabetic Foot Ulcers with Topical Timolol Improves Healed Epithelial Integrity
sources.access_scope: PubMed abstract and metadata; root did not obtain the full journal body in this read.
observations: Post hoc analysis of twenty selected participants whose ulcers had healed, ten per arm.
Lower transepidermal water loss is reported after healing.
No difference in re-ulceration rates was demonstrated in this small study.
sources.interpretation: Selected post-healing barrier observations do not independently establish faster healing or lower recurrence in the randomized population.
limits: Subset selection and parent-trial outcome accounting are separate.
No surrogate-to-clinical-benefit substitution.

sources.title: Beta-adrenergic Antagonist for the Healing of Chronic Diabetic Foot
sources.access_scope: Complete substantive conference abstract; not a full clinical report or statistical analysis plan.
observations: Forty-eight participants were randomized,21timolol and27standard care; the early comparison is8/21 versus7/27 and reported p=0.77.
The text describes7/27 as33%, an arithmetic inconsistency. It shifts between planned week14/31 and reported week15/30 timepoints.
The later unadjusted log-rank p=0.081 differs from a favorable adjusted hazard-ratio result; the latter cannot erase the earlier endpoint finding.
sources.interpretation: The study is a useful contrary check on a broad healing claim, with reporting details requiring registry/full-report reconciliation.
limits: Abstract-only result scope.
No clinical superiority inferred from selected adjusted or post hoc findings.

sources.title: Gpr18 agonist dampens inflammation, enhances myogenesis, and restores muscle function in models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text and figure legends. Root reviewed human-cell readout, muscle-force comparison, biological-unit scope and disclosures.
observations: PSB-KD107 increases absolute and muscle-size-normalized maximal force in treated mdx mice; the functional assessment is ex-vivo muscle force after in-vivo treatment.
The principal force figure reports n=5 except the separate O-1602 comparison n=3.
The human-cell evidence concerns myoblast fusion in dystrophinopathy-derived lines; it is not mature human muscle force.
sources.interpretation: A defined functional preclinical candidate merits a bounded article/exposure/rights review, without inheriting clinical efficacy or a current price.
limits: A patient-cell differentiation result is not a treated-patient result.
No-conflict declaration is not proof of unencumbered rights.
No current license or complete pharmacokinetic/safety package established by this paper.

sources.title: Restoring brain functions in the Mo-blo mouse model of Menkes disease with copper nanoclusters
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text and figure legends; survival, comparator, survivor-selection, residual-function and patent-disclosure passages inspected.
observations: The paper compares copper nanoclusters with copper histidine and untreated Mo-blo mice; reported follow-up reaches fifty days for nanocluster-treated and wild-type animals.
Later behavior is largely compared between nanocluster-treated survivors and wild-type controls after early deaths in other groups, limiting a direct contemporaneous functional efficacy contrast.
Residual motor abnormalities and hepatic/renal marker findings remain relevant; improved survival is not complete neurological or systemic normalization.
Authors disclose WO2022/238656 for the copper-nanocluster family and Menkes use, deposited by Universite de Lorraine.
sources.interpretation: The result is a serious but more complex product proposition whose interpretation must use the current clinical comparator and retain safety/selection uncertainty.
limits: Do not infer a fully observed median lifespan from the fifty-day study boundary.
Patent disclosure is not a current-title, available-license or freedom-to-operate conclusion.
The paper's clinical-status wording must be checked against current primary regulator information.

sources.title: Treatment of Keratin 16 Palmoplantar Keratoderma With Topical Erlotinib — publisher access page
sources.access_scope: Publisher title, metadata and introductory paragraph only; redirected to article-abstract page with GetAccess. Main outcomes not obtained from this read.
observations: The introduction identifies two related patients, mother and son, with KRT16 c.379C>T, p.Arg127Cys hereditary palmoplantar keratoderma.
The intended route is topical erlotinib, distinct from cited systemic treatment for TRPV3 Olmsted syndrome.
sources.interpretation: Confirms exact-use identity and DOI; does not itself verify outcome magnitudes or study phases.
limits: URL containing fullarticle does not imply full-text access.

sources.access_scope: Successful direct API JSON lookup using the installed skill; request contact parameter omitted from public records.
sources.interpretation: No indexed OA copy returned; an independently found lawful public author copy is a separate access route, not an Unpaywall retrieval success.

sources.title: Treatment of Keratin16 Palmoplantar Keratoderma With Topical Erlotinib — public author PDF
sources.access_scope: Both pages of the public author/PC Project PDF, including blinded opposite-foot phases and later uncontrolled extension.
observations: Two related patients, a mother and son with KRT16 Arg127Cys palmoplantar keratoderma, underwent blinded randomized opposite-foot comparisons followed by extension.

The initial lower-strength comparison in the mother had minimal improvement; later treatment with keratolytic support produced a stronger local contrast. Pain-free ambulation was reported during the later uncontrolled bilateral phase.
The son had modest improvement during the controlled phase and later gradual improvement, with limited keratolytic adherence. No adverse effects were reported during the described follow-up.
sources.interpretation: A specific symptomatic local-product hypothesis deserves bounded comparison with inherited local options. Two related cases and cointerventions do not establish general efficacy or a ready commercial product.
limits: No new independent cohort beyond the publisher record.
The strongest functional observation occurred during uncontrolled extension.
Unpaywall returned no OA location; this full text was obtained separately from a public author copy.

sources.title: BAART-DFU NCT03282981 official registry and posted results
sources.access_scope: Complete substantive API JSON, including status, design, outcomes, participant flow and posted result tables.
observations: Forty-eight actual participants were randomized, with 21 assigned to timolol and 27 to standard care plus inactive gel.
The registered primary wound-closure assessment is at 12 weeks; the posted counts are eight of 21 and seven of 27. The registered secondary time-to-closure period is 31 weeks.
Results were first posted on 25 April2025; the record was last updated on 8 May2025.
The conference abstract's 14/15-week early and 30/31-week later descriptions do not match all registered time labels. Its seven of27 equals33% text is also inconsistent.
sources.interpretation: An official result denominator is available. It does not support a definitive healing-superiority claim or allow selected healed-wound barrier findings to replace the randomized primary question.
limits: Registry result tables and the conference abstract describe one parent trial, not independent replications.
No statistical analysis plan, amendments or patient-level data were recovered by root.
The registry labels a primary measure as a percentage but displays counts with participant denominators; interpret the counts explicitly.

sources.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Children With Menkes Disease
sources.access_scope: Complete substantive FDA announcement, including indication, evidence design, population, survival observations and safety summary.
observations: FDA approved Zycubo/copper histidinate for pediatric Menkes disease on12 January2026.
The supporting survival comparison included66 treated children from two open-label single-arm trials and17 untreated contemporaneous external controls.
The announcement reports substantial survival benefit and monitoring for copper toxicity; it does not describe a randomized neurological-function comparison.
sources.interpretation: CuNC development must justify incremental value over an approved copper-histidinate option. An untreated-disease benchmark alone is insufficient to define the current clinical product opportunity.
limits: Approval and clinical survival evidence do not establish that every neurological deficit is corrected.
The FDA date is distinct from sponsor announcements on subsequent dates.
No extrapolation of the human survival effect to the nanocluster formulation.

sources.title: FD-2 ALS paper publisher HTML access attempt
sources.access_scope: Publisher metadata, abstract in metadata and navigation shell; substantive main text not returned by this HTML request.
observations: Metadata distinguishes online publication25 November2025 from January2026 issue date and supplies a public PDF URL.
sources.interpretation: No outcome denominators or detailed methodological conclusions are based on this HTML shell.
limits: A200status and fulltext URL do not demonstrate main-text access.

sources.title: A16-amino acid peptide delays the progression of motor neuron degeneration and pathogenic symptoms in ALS models — full PDF
sources.access_scope: All16pages of the publisher PDF; animal timing, figure denominators, humane endpoint, pharmacokinetic caveat and competing-interest statement inspected.
observations: SOD1-model treatment starts before overt functional decline. Grip and locomotion use five animals per group; the survival analysis uses twelve per group.
The survival measure is time to a humane endpoint, not observed natural lifespan.
The authors identify further pharmacokinetic, degradation and structural work as needed to explain FD-1/FD-2 differences; the proposed stability advantage is not a measured exposure result.
The paper declares no conflict of interest, while a separately recovered patent explicitly names this peptide family.
sources.interpretation: Functional preservation evidence supports a bounded identity/product-rights question. It does not establish post-symptomatic reversal, patient-derived functional rescue or a clinically practical chronic exposure.
limits: Patent and paper examples are related evidence lineages, not automatically independent replication.
Full paper retrieval does not supply current national rights or a licensing offer.

sources.title: US20240327462A1 short-peptide patent publication
sources.access_scope: Full public transcription, nine claims, examples and indexed applicant/family/status fields.
observations: The publication explicitly identifies FD2 and includes its sequence variant in dependent claim5; the claims also address composition and neurological-use scope.
Indexed assignees are Mackay Medical College and Fu Jen Catholic University.
The site labels the US application pending and other family members separately; those indexed labels are not an official current prosecution or title review.
sources.interpretation: A concrete institutional rights question is available. A no-conflict sentence in a paper does not imply an unpatented or unencumbered asset.
limits: No official national prosecution, current ownership chain, enforceability, available license or terms established by this read.
No raw sequences or operational experimental instructions are needed for the investment screen.

sources.title: Sol-Gel second-quarter2026 financial results and corporate update
sources.access_scope: Fresh complete issuer release; SGT-210 program language inspected separately from the principal SGT-610 corporate results.
observations: The issuer states it is continuing an investigational topical EGFR-inhibitor program, SGT-210.
The SGT-210 sentence does not identify KRT16 Arg127Cys, a newly controlled result for the two-patient formulation, or an available license.
sources.interpretation: The local EGFR-product field cannot be assumed vacant. This source does not prove that the exact compounded KRT16 article is company-owned or that a current transaction is available.
limits: A general program statement is not an exact genotype/product claim or new efficacy dataset.
No current agreement, patent-title analysis or commercial terms were inspected.

sources.title: Randomized pilot of DNase eye drops in severe tear-deficient dry eye
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text and displayed tables, including patient flow, study article, controlled symptom/sign comparisons and corneal-staining analysis.
observations: The report describes47 enrolled people and41 completers, with four DNase and two placebo dropouts.
Controlled corneal staining improves, including the reported intent-to-treat analysis. This is distinct from symptoms.
The between-arm OSDI change table reports median changes of minus20.75 for DNase and minus8.43 for vehicle, p=0.078. Within-arm symptom significance is not a controlled symptom-positive result.
The study article is existing recombinant DNase/Pulmozyme used ophthalmically; later proprietary follow-ons cannot inherit exact-article identity automatically.
sources.interpretation: The pilot supports a consequential clinical/product reserve with a stronger ocular-sign result than symptom result. It is not proof of a broadly restored ocular surface or a clear proprietary asset.
limits: Eyes and repeated readings are not independent people.
Small sample, attrition and short follow-up limit safety and clinical certainty.
The paper's historical statement about approved dry-eye drugs is not adopted as current2026 market coverage.
